hints: Start by recalling the exact definition, second ionisation energy must start from one mole of gaseous $\text{Na}^{+}(\text{g})$ ions.
Notice that $X$ removes two electrons from $\text{Na}(\text{g})$, so it contains both the first and second ionisation energies, while $W$ is just the first.
Think about what subtraction will cancel $\text{Na}(\text{g})$ and one electron to leave only $\text{Na}^{+}(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{Na}^{2+}(\text{g}) + \text{e}^{-}$.
walkthrough:
**Recall the definition of second ionisation energy**

Second ionisation energy is the enthalpy change for removing one electron from each ion in one mole of gaseous 1+ ions.

$$\text{Na}^{+}(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{Na}^{2+}(\text{g}) + \text{e}^{-} \quad \Delta H = \text{2nd IE}$$

**Identify what W and X actually mean**

$W$ is the first ionisation energy, starting from $\text{Na}(\text{g})$. $X$ starts from the same $\text{Na}(\text{g})$ but removes two electrons, so it is the sum of first plus second.

$$W: \text{Na}(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{Na}^{+}(\text{g}) + \text{e}^{-}$$
$$X: \text{Na}(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{Na}^{2+}(\text{g}) + 2\text{e}^{-}$$

**Subtract to isolate the second step**

If we take the two-electron change and subtract the one-electron change, the $\text{Na}(\text{g})$ cancels and we are left with the second step only.

$$X - W = [\text{Na}(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{Na}^{2+}(\text{g}) + 2\text{e}^{-}] - [\text{Na}(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{Na}^{+}(\text{g}) + \text{e}^{-}]$$
$$= \text{Na}^{+}(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{Na}^{2+}(\text{g}) + \text{e}^{-}$$

**Match to the options**

That resulting equation is exactly the definition of second ionisation energy, so the value is $X - W$.

options.A: X starts from $\text{Na}(\text{g})$ and forms $\text{Na}^{2+}(\text{g}) + 2\text{e}^{-}$. This is the sum of the first and second ionisation energies together, not the second alone.
options.B: Y is the enthalpy change of atomisation, $\text{Na}(\text{s}) \rightarrow \text{Na}(\text{g})$. There is no need to include the solid state because both W and X already start from $\text{Na}(\text{g})$. Adding Y is a Hess cycle error.
options.C: X minus W removes the first ionisation step from the combined first plus second step. This leaves $\text{Na}^{+}(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{Na}^{2+}(\text{g}) + \text{e}^{-}$, which is exactly the second ionisation energy of sodium.
options.D: Z starts from $\text{Na}(\text{s})$, so $Z = Y + \text{first IE} + \text{second IE}$. Subtracting W only removes the first IE, leaving atomisation plus second IE, not pure second IE. This traps students who forget the state must be gaseous reactant.
